20:1.text: Hear ye this, O house of Jacob, which are called by the name of Israel, and are come forth out of the waters of Judah, which swear by the name of the LORD, and make mention of the God of Israel, but not in truth, nor in righteousness.

provenance.significance: Part of a continuous transcription of Isaiah 48 as 1 Nephi 20. The quotation is not the finding; the departures are, and they are listed in the note and registered individually in data/isaiah-collation.json.

20:1.note: 3 departure(s) from the KJV: adds “Hearken and”; KJV “ye” omitted; KJV “but” → “yet they swear”. The 1830 has no baptismal clause here. The 1840 edition inserted “or out of the waters of baptism” after “out of the waters of Judah”, and modern editions keep it; the first edition does not, so the running text of this catalogue reproduces Isaiah 48:1 with only the additions listed above.

20:2.text: For they call themselves of the holy city, and stay themselves upon the God of Israel; The LORD of hosts is his name.

provenance.significance: Part of a continuous transcription of Isaiah 48 as 1 Nephi 20. The quotation is not the finding; the departures are, and they are listed in the note and registered individually in data/isaiah-collation.json.

20:2.note: 3 departure(s) from the KJV: KJV “For” → “Nevertheless”; KJV “and” → “but they do not”; adds “which is the Lord of hosts yea”. The chapter's largest theological addition in its opening: Isaiah's flat “for they call themselves of the holy city” becomes “Nevertheless … but they do not stay themselves upon the God of Israel, which is the Lord of hosts”. Isaiah reports the claim; the Book of Mormon denies it in the same breath.

20:10.note: 2 departure(s) from the KJV: adds “For”; KJV “but not with silver” omitted. KJV Isaiah 48:10 reads “I have refined thee, but not with silver”. Note for the italics question below: “but not with silver” is not italicized in the KJV, so this omission is not explained by the usual italics hypothesis.

20:14.note: 3 departure(s) from the KJV: adds “unto them”; adds “yea and he will fulfil his word which he hath declared by them and”; KJV “be on” → “come upon”. The longest addition in the chapter: fourteen words inserted into Isaiah's oracle about the LORD's beloved doing his pleasure on Babylon — “yea, and he will fulfil his word which he hath declared by them”. The insertion makes the prophets, not Cyrus, the agent.

This is the verse Lehi spoke over Laman and Lemuel at the river at 1 Nephi 2:9-10, seventeen chapters earlier, in his own words; here the family reads it out as scripture. 20:21.text: And they thirsted not when he led them through the deserts: he caused the waters to flow out of the rock for them: he clave the rock also, and the waters gushed out.

provenance.significance: Part of a continuous transcription of Isaiah 48 as 1 Nephi 20. The quotation is not the finding; the departures are, and they are listed in the note and registered individually in data/isaiah-collation.json.

20:21.note: 2 departure(s) from the KJV: KJV “when” omitted; KJV “clave” → “cleaved”. Hardy points the two wilderness water-from-the-rock narratives (Exodus 17:1-7, Numbers 20:2-13) at this verse, and Isaiah 48:21 is their poetic recollection: “he caused the waters to flow out of the rock for them; he clave the rock also and the waters gushed out.” Nephi had made the same recital in his own words at 17:29, where the link to those chapters is argued; here he reads it out as Isaiah.

20:22.note: 1 departure(s) from the KJV: adds “And notwithstanding he hath done all this and greater also”. The chapter's closing addition, and its sharpest: Isaiah ends “There is no peace, saith the LORD, unto the wicked.” The Book of Mormon prefixes “And notwithstanding he hath done all this, and greater also” — which converts a verdict into a complaint about ingratitude.
